summary: Phramonchai Saitanaporn is a Buddhist studies scholar. He earned a PhD from the University of Sydney, attested in 2009 under doctoral supervisor Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle, and also studied under traditional teacher Phrathepyanmahamuni.

Phuntshok Tashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned a BA at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, an MA at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, and held a post at the National Museum of Bhutan.

Phyllis Granoff is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard (~1969–1973). She held professorships at McMaster University (~1976–2004) and Yale University (~2004), among other appointments.

Pierce Salguero specializes in Buddhist studies, history/archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at the University of Virginia (~1992–1996, ~2003–2005) and Johns Hopkins University (~2005–2010), holding posts at Pennsylvania State University (2010) and University of Pennsylvania (2011–2012).

Linguist Pierre Amédée Jaubert studied at the École nationale des langues orientales vivantes (~1795–1798), later serving there (~1820–1847), at the Collège de France (1838–1847), and as president of the Société Asiatique (1834–1847).
Pieter Cornelis Verhagen works in Tibetology, Indology, and linguistics. He completed his PhD at Leiden University by 1991 and served there as a research fellow, attested in 1996.
Pieter Hendrik Pott worked in Tibetology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He was a curator at the Museum Volkenkunde (~1947–1965) and held a post at Leiden University in 1973.
Linguist Pietro Merlo studied at the University of Turin (~1868–1872) under Giovanni Flechia (~1869–1872). He later held an academic appointment at the University of Pavia (~1881–1888).

Indologist and philosopher Piotr Balcerowicz studied at Banaras Hindu University, the University of Warsaw, the University of Hamburg, and the Polish Academy of Sciences. He also held an editorial post at the University of Warsaw (attested 2000–2004).

Piotr Klafkowski was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who earned a PhD at Adam Mickiewicz University under Jerzy Bańczerowski. He also studied under Lobsang Jamspal, Geshe Geleg Gyatsho, Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche, and Nyalo Trulku Jampa Kelzang Rinpoche.
Poerbatjaraka was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and history/archaeology. He studied at Leiden University (~1920–1926) and held a post at the University of Indonesia (~1950–1964).

Poh Beng Tan works in Buddhist studies, earning an MA at the International Buddhist College (attested 2015) under supervisors Charles Willemen and Tilak Kariyawasam. He also studied under teachers Sumanasiri and Shengshou.

Polly Young-Eisendrath is a scholar in Buddhist studies and other fields. She completed her studies at Ohio University (~1967–1969), Goddard College (~1970–1971), and Washington University in St. Louis (~1974–1980).

Pori Park specializes in Buddhist studies and religious studies, having studied under Robert E. Buswell Jr. She held a position as assistant professor of religious studies at Arizona State University.

Prabal Kumar Sen is a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held a professorship at the University of Calcutta, attested in 2009, and also held an appointment at the Ramakrishna Mission Institute of Culture.

Prabodh Chandra Bagchi was an Indologist, sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Sylvain Lévi at the University of Paris. He held posts at the University of Calcutta (1930–1944), Peking University (1947), and Visva-Bharati University (1954–1956).

Prafulla Chandra Ray was a scholar of history/archaeology and Indology who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1882–1888). He held posts at Presidency University, Kolkata (1911–1916) and University College of Science, Technology & Agriculture (1916–1936).

Prahlad Pradhan worked in Indology and Buddhist studies, studying at Visva-Bharati and Patna Universities. He held positions at Visva-Bharati (~1939–1945), Utkal University (attested 1971–1975), Gangadhar Meher University, Ravenshaw College, and Shri Jagannath Sanskrit University.

Pramod Chandra was a scholar of history/archaeology and Indology who studied at Georgetown University. He held academic posts at the University of Chicago (~1963–1980) and as a professor at Harvard University (~1980–2003).
Prapod Assavavirulhakarn is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Chulalongkorn University (attested 1998) and Ryukoku University (attested 2014).
